title: Per-directional IO floor with windowed streaming grace and contract exceptions experiment
creator: Aisha Chen
description:
Objective: Validate a hybrid pricing experiment that decouples ingress (input) and egress (output) token rates with asymmetric per-direction floors, plus a short-window streaming grace that credits low-duration streaming sessions. We will also test a contract-exception path for large enterprises that require custom minimums documented in their security questionnaire (SQ) or contract.

Background: Customers are asking for clearer alignment between token directionality and unit economics: generative chat-heavy apps create disproportionate output tokens; embedding-heavy pipelines create mostly input tokens. Existing symmetric floors bias billing for some workloads. We want to evaluate whether directional floors + a short streaming grace window (to avoid penalizing brief conversational sessions) reduces churn and improves revenue predictability without negatively impacting adoption.

Hypotheses:
- H1: Directional floors (higher floor on output tokens than input) will reduce unexpected overage complaints for chat-heavy customers and increase effective revenue per active customer by ~6-10% for chat workloads.
- H2: A windowed streaming grace (e.g., credit first N seconds or first M streamed tokens per session) will reduce trial friction and lower aborted session rate by 8-12% for interactive demos.
- H3: Offering a contract-exception flow (special floors or temporary waivers) will accelerate large enterprise contract closures with minimal incremental leakage when gated by legal/SQ approvals.

Experiment design:
- Arms: (A) Baseline symmetric pricing (control); (B) Directional floors: input floor = 0.6*baseline, output floor = 1.2*baseline with same per-token rates; (C) Directional floors + streaming grace window (first 30s or first 400 streamed tokens credited up to floor); (D) Enterprise-contract exception funnel (manual mapping for 10 inbound enterprise trials).
- Sample: Randomized new accounts + opt-in existing customers (A/B allocation) across regions: US/EU primary; APAC holdout for later validation.
- Duration: 6 weeks live, 3 weeks ramp, 3 weeks measurement.
- Metrics: activation rate (first week), churn at 30/60 days, gross revenues per cohort, ARPU, disputes / billing tickets, average session length for streaming calls, percent of sessions fully credited by grace window, net-new enterprise contract wins attributed to exception flow.
- Success criteria: statistically significant (>90% CI) improvement in revenue per active customer without >5% increase in billing disputes or customer support volume, and <2% revenue leakage from enterprise exceptions over baseline forecast.

Implementation notes / infra requirements:
- Billing: needs directional token metering implemented server-side. Feature flag gating for per-customer floors. (Dependency: ENG-20421 billing metering patch).
- Streaming grace: ephemeral session id tagging and short-lived credit ledger (stateless + idempotency). (Dependency: ENG-21780 streaming-session-metrics).
- Console: new dashboard tile showing directional floor exposure and streaming-grace credits consumed. (Design input requested from DES-142).
- Legal/Sales: create SQ/contract exception form and triage workflow. Sales to provide 10 candidate enterprise pilots.

Telemetry & queries (primary):
- BigQuery: billing.events partitioned by day: compute per-account ingress_tokens, egress_tokens, applied_floor, and grace_credits. Example query link: https://bigquery.redwood.ai/samples/pricing_experiments/directional_floor_baseline
- Dashboards: experiment cohort breakdown (activation, ARPU, disputes) in Looker: dashboard-pricing/directional-floor-2026.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag deploy to canary accounts (internal + 50 external beta) — week 1.
2) Enable randomized allocation for selected sample (week 2 ramp). Guardrails: limit to 10% of active new signups.
3) Monitor KPIs daily; weekly review with infra, billing, and support owners.
4) If no major regressions after 6 weeks, extend to 30% sample and prepare pricing docs and SDK updates.

Monitoring & rollback conditions:
- Immediate rollback if billing anomalies >0.5% of daily revenue or a 50%+ increase in billing disputes for experiment cohorts.
- Pause expansion if streaming latency or session errors increase >15% relative to control.

Open questions / risks:
- Edge cases: multi-tenant apps that proxy many end-users will need a clear guidance doc to avoid cross-account aggregation gaming the grace window.
- Accounting alignment: need to reconcile directional floors for GAAP revenue recognition with Finance.
- Sales incentives: enterprise AEs might request broad exceptions; define strict SLA/contract guardrails to limit leakage.
